messages:
incident-bot: paging oncall tim: Severity=sev2, alert: runtime-node-3 high OOM rate during warmup for model-llama-13b-v2. Instance flapping and multiple container crashes detected.

tim: I’m on it. grabbing logs and checking node health.

sanjay: i’m awake too, will pull /var/log/redwood/inference.log and kernel logs. can someone confirm customer impact?

maria: - Customer impact: increased 5xxs for Hosted customers using model-llama-13b-v2 in us-west1. Some requests degraded to fallback small-model. No data exfil.

ashley: seeing repeated failures at model load step: "deserialize: KV cache alloc failed: cannot allocate 16GB" followed by "cudaErrorIllegalAddress" and container restart.

kevin: also a number of nodes hit OOM during `model_compile` stage: "compile timeout after 180s" for several kernels. Looks like JIT compile got stuck and memory spiked.

jess: ops-bot noted node flaps: node-03 entered NotReady 6x in last 12m. kubelet restarts coincide with container restarts.

tim: ok mitigation plan attempt 1: 1) stop warmup-on-deploy for the model to prevent cascading loads 2) divert new inference traffic for that model to model-llama-7b-fallback in the routing layer 3) cordon+drain node-03 with graceful timeout 2m 4) escalate if drain fails.

sanjay: commands I’m running:
```
ssh root@node-03
journalctl -u redwood-inference -n 200 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
kubectl cordon node-03
kubectl drain node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=300s
```

maria: routing changes applied: new requests for model-llama-13b-v2 get 503->fallback and are transparently routed to 7b-fallback. Traffic reduced by ~78% to affected nodes. Verified in console: per-route throughput for 13b dropped.

ashley: logs from container before crash:
```
[WARN] model_loader: loading weights shard 2/8
[ERROR] deserializer: kv_deserialize failed: corrupted header
[ERROR] allocator: out of memory while reserving 12.1GB
[CRIT] runtime: cudart error: illegal memory access at 0x7fffae9b0000
```

kevin: that deserializer error could be a bad checkpoint shard or memory layout mismatch after quantization. But we also see compile timeout which suggests heavy compile jitter.

tim: mitigation attempt 2 (safe): 1) disable eager compilation for this model to avoid large one-time compile spikes 2) enable `--load-no-compile` flag on new loads 3) increase model cache backoff to prevent simultaneous warmups.

jess: I pushed a temporary config change to the control-plane: 
- model.warmup.strategy = "serial"
- model.compile.eager = false
- warmup.concurrent_limit = 1

ops-bot: automated action: redirected 85% traffic of model-llama-13b-v2 to fallback route as configured by tim.

sanjay: I performed a manual load with flags to reproduce guarded load:
```
redwoodctl model prewarm --model model-llama-13b-v2 --no-compile --disable-kv-cache
```
Result: model loaded into memory (weights mapped) but skipped compile; host memory usage stable. No immediate OOM.

ashley: interestingly, when we allow compile after load on a node with smaller concurrent load, the compile finishes but at higher memory transient. We need to tune compile cache and kernel build timeouts.

maria: Customer impact update: Some customers on Dedicated saw increased latency (p95 up from 180ms to 1.2s) and a small % of requests failed with 502 during the span. We've opened a ticket with the largest affected customer and offered rollback to previous model variant.

kevin: I recommend increasing compile timeout to 10m for this stage in the short term and bumping compile cache size to 40GB on the node pool for these models.

tim: We should be cautious increasing default timeouts. Instead do targeted nodepool with larger compile cache and run builds there. Plan: create compile-heavy node pool (gpu-compile-1), cordon old nodes for cleanup, migrate warmups to the compile pool.

jess: created node pool gpu-compile-1 with 4 nodes (A100s) and tainted them for compile=allowed. Pushing a one-off rollout to prewarm on those nodes.

ops-bot: action: scheduled model warmup job on gpu-compile-1, job id warmup-212345.

sanjay: warmup job logs show progress: compile steps started earlier and are finishing, no deserializer errors. Memory transient peaks but within node limits.

ashley: to prevent future deserialization-corruption suspicion, I verified checksum of shards in object store: all OK. So corruption improbable. Looks like memory pressure + deserialize race.

tim: handoff notes for morning oncall:
- issue: model-llama-13b-v2 warmup triggered OOMs & cuda illegal addr -> node flaps and container crashes. Root cause likely combined: heavy eager compilation + simultaneous warmups + memory fragmentation during KV deserialization.
- mitigations applied: traffic routed to fallback 7b, node-03 cordoned/drained, warmup concurrency reduced to 1, eager compilation disabled, compile pool created (gpu-compile-1) and warmups moved there, temporary compile timeout increase for warmup jobs.
- customer impact: elevated 5xx and latency for some hosted and dedicated customers; notified affected customers and offered rollback.
- next steps: monitor compile pool health for 6h, evaluate increasing compile cache size permanently, add guardrail to prevent >N simultaneous compilations per cluster, add early-memory-check in deserializer to fail fast if allocation cannot be satisfied.

maria: additional note: cluster autoscaler triggered scale-up earlier and that may have contributed to concurrent warmups starting at same time. We'll add jitter to auto-provision warmups.

kevin: follow-up engineering ticket: INF-1987 "Guardrails for model compile & warmup" assigned to eng-runtime. Includes: compile cache metrics, per-model warmup limits, safer deserializer memory accounting, retries with backoff.

jess: leaving logs and commands in incident doc. Will keep alerting thresholds throttled to avoid noisy pages overnight.

tim: handing off to morning oncall (sanjay, you're point). If anything flips back to sev1, ping #pager immediately and call. Summary posted to incident board. ttyl. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: ack, I’ll monitor next 4 hours and verify customer ticket statuses. Thanks team.

incident-bot: incident 2123456789 updated: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, owner=sanjay, link=https://redwood.incidents/2123456789
